text_blocks.snippet: Federal prosecutors and state authorities warn of a surge in active phone spoofing and text message scams targeting Central Illinois residents.

list.snippet: The Scheme: Scammers spoof official phone numbers for the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of Illinois and use staff names to demand money.
The Reality: Federal prosecutors never request payment or sensitive data over the phone.
The Scheme: Fraudulent texts claim unpaid tolls or traffic tickets threaten immediate license suspension.
The Reality: The Illinois Secretary of State never texts demands for payment or fine warnings.
The Scheme: Callers falsely claim a family member is in custody and demand bond money via prepaid gift cards.
The Reality: Illinois has eliminated cash bail, and legitimate bond fees are never paid via gift cards.
Don't Click: Never tap links or QR codes in unsolicited texts.
Verify Independently: Hang up and call official agency numbers directly.
Report Fraud: Forward suspicious DMV texts to scamalert@ilsos.gov.
